'''Edward W. Kolb''', known as '''Rocky Kolb''', (born October 2, 1951) is a [[Physical cosmology|cosmologist]] and a professor at the [[University of Chicago]] as well as the dean of [[Physical Sciences]]. He has worked on many aspects of the [[Big Bang]] cosmology, including [[baryogenesis]], [[Big Bang nucleosynthesis|nucleosynthesis]] and [[dark matter]]. He is author, with [[Michael Turner (cosmologist)|Michael Turner]], of the popular textbook ''The Early Universe'' (Addison-Wesley, 1990). Additionally, alongside his co-author Michael Turner, Kolb was awarded the 2010 [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Astrophysics]].<ref>{{Citation | title = Grants, Prizes, and Awards | url = http://aas.org/grants/awards.php#heineman | accessdate = 10 February 2010 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20101222143439/http://www.aas.org/grants/awards.php#heineman | archivedate = 22 December 2010 }}</ref>

Kolb's collaborators also include [[Stephen Wolfram]]<ref>{{cite journal| url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0550321380901674 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(80)90167-4 | title=Baryon number generation in the early universe | date=1980 | last1=Kolb | first1=Edward W. | last2=Wolfram | first2=Stephen | journal=Nuclear Physics B | volume=172 | pages=224–284 | bibcode=1980NuPhB.172..224K | url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[Richard Slansky]].<ref>{{cite journal| url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269384902983 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(84)90298-3 | title=Dimensional reduction in the early universe: Where have the massive particles gone? | date=1984 | last1=Kolb | first1=Edward W. | last2=Slansky | first2=Richard | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=135 | issue=5–6 | pages=378–382 | bibcode=1984PhLB..135..378K | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He received the [[Quantrell Award]].<ref name="Prize">{{cite web|title=Llewellyn John and Harriet Manchester Quantrell Awards for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching|url=https://www.uchicago.edu/who-we-are/global-impact/accolades/llewellyn-john-and-harriet-manchester-quantrell-awards-for-excellence-in-undergraduate-teaching|website=UChicago}}</ref>

He is married to [[Adrienne Kolb]], a [[history of science|historian of science]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://news.fnal.gov/2015/06/adrienne-kolb-retires/|title=Adrienne Kolb retires|date=June 23, 2015|first=Valerie|last=Higgins|publisher=Fermilab|access-date=June 27, 2020|archive-date=February 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202110745/https://news.fnal.gov/2015/06/adrienne-kolb-retires/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and has three children.<ref name=cv/>
